title: Weapons: WS integration — A fires at B, B's shields drop, C sees the FX events
description: New app/src/server/shard/shard.weapons.ws.test.ts: the TASK-43 integration acceptance criterion ('ship A fires at B, B's shields drop, C sees the FX events') over REAL websocket clients. Model it on the committed app/src/server/shard/shard.combat.ws.test.ts (same beforeAll/afterAll shape: tmpdir sqlite, buildServer, attachWebSocket with createRegistryGateway, claim via POST /api/callsigns, WsTestClient + joinSystem from @server/ws-test-client, teleportForTesting both ships 60 km out, 400 ms wait for the regime re-resolve to 'space'). The one wiring difference from the combat test: its onGameMessage is a no-op — here it must route 'fire' frames to shard.handleFire, so the fire INTENT travels over the wire exactly like production (routeGameMessage in @server/shards does this at runtime). The server fire pipeline is already committed and unit-tested — this task is a test file only, no production changes unless a real bug is exposed (then fix minimally with this test as the regression).

steps.details: Copy the structure of shard.combat.ws.test.ts verbatim (env object with a fresh GALAXY_SEED like 'weapons-ws-seed-001', tmpdir + createDb + createRepo + sqliteTables, createTokenCodec/createSessionService/createTokenAuthenticate, createShipSwapBus, generateStars/generateSystem + repo.upsertSystem, new SystemShard + shard.start(), buildServer + registerApiRoutes, attachWebSocket, app.listen({port: 0}), claim() via POST /api/callsigns, join() via WsTestClient + joinSystem + the 100×20 ms entity-wait loop). The ONLY behavioral difference: pass onGameMessage: (conn, type, payload) => { if (type === 'fire' && conn.playerId) shard.handleFire(conn.playerId, payload as { weapon: string; targetId?: string }, conn); } (mirror the production routeGameMessage branch, shards.ts — keep the same payload shape). Scenario 1 (laser, one 'it'): three clients A/B/C (C fires nothing — the observer, exactly like the combat test's 'Combat-Charlie'); teleport A and B 60 km out via shard.teleportForTesting (the combat test's POS_A/POS_B pattern, e.g. 60 m apart in open space); wait 400 ms; assert both regimes 'space'. A sends client.send({ v: PROTOCOL_VERSION, type: 'fire', payload: { weapon: 'laser', targetId: b.shipId } }) — PROTOCOL_VERSION is the shared const (import it; it is 1). Assert: (a) B's shard-state shields drop to 1 − 8/50 within a bounded wait (poll shard.entities, same 20 ms loop as join()); (b) C receives combat_event {kind:'laser-fired'} and then {kind:'hit', target: b.shipId, weapon:'laser', damage: 8} IN ORDER on its socket (c.client.next(...) + the isCombat filter pattern from the combat test); (c) A's energy: the ship docks at a pad on join with energy undefined → the first tick materializes it to 100, so one accepted laser fire costs 2 — assert the post-fire value accounting for 0.5 u/50 ms tick regen (e.g. read immediately, or allow the regen band; do NOT assert 'stays undefined').

Scenario 2 (missile, second 'it' — fresh clients or the same ones with a cooldown wait): A fires { weapon: 'missile', targetId: b.shipId } at a stationary B in open space within 800 m (keep A→B ≤ ~300 m so the homing missile hits well inside its 5 s ttl: at 120 u/s a straight target is contacted in ~2.5 s at 300 m). Assert C observes 'missile-fired', then 'missile-impact', then 'hit' (damage 25, B's shields → 1 − 25/50) in order on its socket, and that the projectile is a real ENTITY: while in flight (poll right after the fire) shard.entities contains a kind:'projectile' entity, and it is GONE after impact/expiry. Scenario 3 (denied fire shows nothing): A fires a laser or missile with no valid target (targetId of a destroyed/absent ship, or an out-of-range/no-LOS setup) — assert NO combat_event reaches C for that fire and A's energy is unchanged at the post-regen baseline (silent drop / refund contract — 'energy not spent on denied fires'). Do not over-build: these three scenarios are the AC; rate-limit/energy/lock unit tests already exist in shard.weapons.test.ts and are NOT repeated here.

cd app && npx vitest run src/server/shard/shard.weapons.ws.test.ts → green (fresh run); re-run the two unit files once to confirm no cross-talk (npx vitest run src/shared/weapons.test.ts src/server/shard/shard.weapons.test.ts, expect 33/33 — they should be green from TASK-43.1); npx tsc --noEmit clean; npx eslint --fix + npx prettier --write on the new file; commit with a Conventional Commit message (e.g. 'test(weapons): TASK-43.2 fire pipeline over live ws — A fires, B shields drop, C observes'). If a scenario exposes a REAL server bug (e.g. the fire frame is not routed, or an event is missing on the observer's socket), fix the production code minimally, keep the test as the regression, and re-run the weapons unit files + this ws file. If time runs short before step 2 completes, commit step 1 (laser scenario green) and leave an updated .ralph/handoff/TASK-43.md naming exactly what remains (the missile + denied scenarios).

acceptanceCriteria: app/src/server/shard/shard.weapons.ws.test.ts exists and mirrors shard.combat.ws.test.ts (same env/tmpdir/buildServer/attachWebSocket/claim/join shape, three live WsTestClients); the fire INTENT is sent over the wire ({ v: PROTOCOL_VERSION, type: 'fire', payload: { weapon, targetId? } }) and routed through onGameMessage → shard.handleFire, not called directly

Laser AC green: A fires at B, B's shields drop to 1 − 8/50 (shard state, observed via the polling pattern), and C — which fires nothing — receives 'laser-fired' then 'hit' combat_events in order on its own socket

Missile scenario green: C observes 'missile-fired' → 'missile-impact' → 'hit' (damage 25) in order; the projectile exists as a kind:'projectile' entity in shard.entities while in flight and is gone afterwards
Denied fire: no combat_event reaches C for the denied fire and A's energy is unchanged (silent drop / refund — nothing spent on a denied fire)

cd app && npx vitest run src/server/shard/shard.weapons.ws.test.ts green on a fresh run; the 33 weapon unit tests stay green; npx tsc --noEmit clean; eslint + prettier clean; committed with a Conventional Commit message
notes: BUILD ON TASK-43.1: by the time this task starts, all 33 weapon unit tests (18 shared + 15 shard) are green and committed, including the previously-failing ridge-LOS test. The working tree should be clean (git status); if TASK-43.1 left a WIP commit or an updated handoff, follow it and finish its step 3 first (commit) before starting this task.

WHAT IS ALREADY COMMITTED (do not re-derive): the whole fire pipeline — shard.handleFire (loadout check, per-weapon cooldown, energy check that deducts ONLY on accepted fires, range/LOS via TASK-42, 30-fires/s → weapon-locked for 5 s {code:'weapon-locked'}, silent rate-limit drops), fireLaser (broadcasts 'laser-fired' BEFORE the contact hit, resolves at the first valid target or the terrain occlusion point), fireMissile + the sim's projectile tick (homing turnToward capped 1.5 rad/s, speed 120 u/s, ttl 5 s, 16-cap with oldest-expired-first, 5 m splash: 25 to target / 12 to others, friendly fire ON), validMissileTarget + energy REFUND when the target is lost between acceptance and tick. Client FX + #weapon-hud are also committed but are NOT exercised here (that is TASK-43.3's e2e).

THE ONE WIRING DIFFERENCE vs the combat test (this is the crux — get it right first): shard.combat.ws.test.ts passes onGameMessage: () => {} (comment: 'combat has no inbound traffic: fire intents (TASK-43) only') and calls shard.handleWeaponContact DIRECTLY. This test replaces that no-op with the production routing: if (type === 'fire' && conn.playerId) shard.handleFire(conn.playerId, payload as { weapon: string; targetId?: string }, conn). Production does this in routeGameMessage (app/src/server/shards.ts, the 'fire' branch) — copy its payload cast.

CLASS/VEHICLE FACT (solved — do not re-derive): ships claimed via POST /api/callsigns are 'scout' (routes/callsigns.ts), loadout laser-only — a scout CANNOT fire missiles (loadout gate). Do NOT go through the buy/swap REST flow for an interceptor. The proven cheap path is the one the unit tests use (shard.weapons.test.ts shipAt helper): mutate the shard entity directly after join — `shard.entities.get(a.shipId)!.classId = 'interceptor'` — then A's fire of { weapon: 'missile' } passes the loadout gate. handleFire re-derives everything from the entity on each fire, so the mutation is honored. (A denied-fire scenario can then double as the loadout-gate-over-ws check: a SECOND scout client firing a missile gets a silent drop.)
ENVIRONMENT FACTS (from the combat test + attempts): ships claimed via POST /api/callsigns dock at the pad on join with energy UNDEFINED → the first sim tick materializes it to 100 (full).

REGIME + TIMING: teleportForTesting + 400 ms wait → both ships 'space' (beyond the 1050 m atmosphere exit radius) — terrain/LOS is skipped in space, so NO ridge hunting is needed here (contrast TASK-43.1's unit test). The sim runs at 20 Hz (50 ms ticks); a laser resolves on the NEXT tick after the fire frame, so bound the observer waits at 5000 ms like the combat test. The 10 Hz entity_update carries B's dropped shields to B's own socket eventually — but assert the SHARD STATE for the damage (the event stream is the AC for C, the state is the AC for B), matching the handoff's guidance.

ENERGY MATH: laser costs 2, regen 10/s = 0.5 per 50 ms tick. Assert exactly, or with the regen band, IMMEDIATELY after the fire resolves — never assert 'energy stays undefined' after any tick (the first tick materializes 100).
AFTER THIS TASK: TASK-43.3 (e2e laser flash in the browser + screenshot + full npm run test + lint + TASK-43 bookkeeping/close-out + <promise>TASK-43:DONE</promise>).

IF A PRODUCTION BUG IS EXPOSED: fix minimally in app/src/server/ (the fire frame routing, the event broadcast to all in-system conns including the shooter, or the projectile entity lifecycle) — the weapons unit tests must stay green; this ws file becomes the regression. Do NOT refactor.
